publicApiReproduction.operations: One manager; repeated MrmGetChildResourceMap and MrmGetResourceCount for the same resource, then MrmDestroyResourceManager; module kept loaded for census.
publicApiReproduction.measurement: Locked default-process HeapWalk counts busy 104-byte blocks matching the returned vtable. No UI, managed projection or hardware calls.
publicApiReproduction.conclusion: The pinned binary retains a subtree per lookup through manager destruction, independently of WinUI and application subscriptions.

applicationOwnerEvidence.observed: Four sampled four-byte ID allocations are referenced by these fields in symbol-identified native subtrees; not a census of every retained byte.

upstreamSource.relationshipToBinary: Source corroboration; these revisions are not established build provenance of the measured DLLs.

references.finding: GetSubtree creates a new allocation and detaches ownership; its destructor would release descendant arrays.
Child-map API returns that pointer; manager state and destruction have no matching child-subtree ownership list.
Projection destructor is empty and assigns map ownership to the resource manager.
XAML property-bag lookup obtains the main map, a subtree and its resource count; this supports the UID-localization path as an allocation source, without an allocation-stack capture.

events.interpretation: Stepped increase followed by a plateau, not one Event leak per language change.

longRun.interpretation: HeapWalk busy means allocated, not proven reachable. Default-heap data exclude other heaps, GC and mappings; free capacity is not live application payload.

windowing.countOfEachType: 12 + 2 * completed language changes at every sampled batch; 396 of each after 192 changes and idle.
windowing.managedObservation: Separate earlier 70-change dump: no AppWindowChangedEventArgs RCW instances, with event infrastructure still present. Not the 192-change process or proof against every managed owner.
